---
title: CLI
---

Run the installed command through uv:

```sh
uv run restic-backups
```

In an interactive terminal, running without a command opens a described
arrow-key menu for **Generic backups**, **Voice Memos**, and configuration
validation. Each workflow opens another described arrow-key menu. Explicit
subcommands remain available for scripts and scheduled jobs.

Every menu level includes **Help** and **Back**. **Help** shows the commands and
flags for the current level, then returns to the same menu; it does not load the
configuration or contact remote storage.

Press Escape to return to the previous menu. Press Ctrl+C at any prompt to exit
the TUI cleanly.

Show command-line help instead:

```sh
uv run restic-backups --help
```

Commands that use a repository require a configuration file. Pass the global
options before the command:

```sh
uv run restic-backups --config config.yaml generic repository list
uv run restic-backups --config config.sops.yaml --sops generic backup list
```

The equivalent environment variables are `RESTIC_BACKUPS_CONFIG` and
`RESTIC_BACKUPS_SOPS=1`. See [Configuration](configuration.qmd) for setup.

Commands use colored, level-aware stderr logging for configuration and operation
progress. Add `--verbose` before the command, or set
`RESTIC_BACKUPS_VERBOSE=1`, to include command-level details without printing
credentials or repository passwords:

```sh
uv run restic-backups --verbose generic repository init
```

## Audit log

Command auditing is enabled by default. `restic-backups` appends one compact
JSON object per line to `audit-log.json` in the directory where it was started.
Each record contains:

- `date-time`: the UTC date and time;
- `hostname`: the machine hostname;
- `command`: the executable or CLI command;
- `args`: its arguments.

The file uses one JSON object per line so new records can be appended without
rewriting existing records. It is created with owner-only permissions (`0600`).
Interactive selections are recorded when run, and restic subprocess records
contain the exact raw restic arguments, including generated repository options.
Credentials and repository passwords are passed through the environment rather
than arguments. Values attached to password-, secret-, token-, credential-, and
key-like arguments are replaced with `[REDACTED]`.

The log can still reveal repository names and local paths. Keep it private and
rotate or archive it according to your own retention policy. To turn auditing
off explicitly:

```sh
export RESTIC_BACKUPS_AUDIT=0
```

The values `false`, `no`, and `off` are also accepted, case-insensitively.

## Root commands

| Command | Purpose | Repository access |
|---|---|---|
| `check-config` | Load and validate configuration | No |
| `generic ...` | Run generic configured repository commands | Depends on subcommand |
| `voice-memos ...` | Run the macOS Voice Memos workflow | Depends on subcommand |

Use [Generic Backups](generic.qmd) for restic passthrough, repository
initialization, restores, and managed data directories. Use
[Voice Memos Backups](voice-memos.qmd) for the macOS-specific workflow.

Run subcommand help without loading a configuration:

```sh
uv run restic-backups generic --help
uv run restic-backups voice-memos --help
```
